brief: JPMorgan reports positive US leading indicators and S&P 500 earnings revisions at the high end of history, driven by hyperscaler results: AWS revenue up 37%, Azure 43%, Google Cloud 82%, with backlogs rising. Cembalest argues earnings growth is contingent on hyperscaler capital spending and R&D, which rose from $460 bn in 2024 to $870 bn over 12 months, because earnings breadth has outrun the ISM survey that normally predicts it, implying trickle-down from hyperscalers, and because an unusually high share of S&P 500 earnings comes from unrealized valuation gains on Anthropic and OpenAI. He then argues Treasury cannot easily cap 10 year yields: growth is strong relative to Fed Funds, deficits worsen, and hyperscaler long duration issuance is 68% of new Treasury long duration borrowing, so the August Twist left the 10 year yield above its announcement level. The remainder is a post-mortem on a year of calls, claiming hits (healthcare, hyperscaler stagnation, semiconductor peak, software oversold, no SMR renaissance, stable dollar, Oracle overpriced, Fed to hike, media risk) and misses (China AI, Chicago default risk, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, US small cap, Asian and EM fixed income, critical minerals), then raises questions about Mamdani's NYC property seizure plan.
